note: Phase 0.11 Workstream Z1 — the cross-language drift guard for the part-number resolver. Neither language owns this file. `src/lib/partNumber.contract.test.ts` asserts the TypeScript resolver (buildPartNumber in src/lib/summary.ts, the reference implementation) produces `expected`; `geometry-service/tests/test_partnumber.py` asserts the Python mirror (app/partnumber.py) produces the same strings from the same catalog. Changing resolution behaviour in one language breaks the other's suite until both are updated together — which is the entire point, and is what 0.10.5 lost when it dropped the Python side.
regenerate: UPDATE_PN_CASES=1 npx vitest run src/lib/partNumber.contract.test.ts — rewrites only the `expected` blocks, from the TypeScript resolver. Review the diff: a change here is a change to a customer-facing SKU.
expectedIsNullWhen: The selected part has no machine-parsed ordering sheet and no modelCodes, so it resolves to NO part number at all (rendered as 'part number pending matrix'). Never a fabricated code — see docs/part-numbers.md.

cases.name: default WiLLstudio assembly, nothing configured
cases.why: Every ordering column unanswered still yields a number with '_' placeholders, so the baseline shape is pinned.

cases.name: GVX with every ordering column chosen
cases.why: The full happy path: the fixture sheet's own ordering example must reproduce exactly.

cases.name: per-slot finishes (Workstream A)
cases.why: Each component's own finish must drive its own finish segment — the headline 0.11 behaviour, and the reason config_hash had to learn about `finishes`.

cases.name: anodized finish drives the pole's finish-type segment
cases.why: finish-type is derived from the picked colour (FP painted / AN anodized), never a dropdown.

cases.name: custom RAL on the pole
cases.why: custom-ral is a real palette entry with code RAL — it must resolve, not fall through to '_'.

cases.name: arm model code follows the radial count
cases.why: Arms with modelCodes resolve straight to the official code for that count (SS3 = 3 arms), bypassing the column walk.

cases.name: arm has no model code for the requested count
cases.why: SH1 is single-only; asking for 3 must yield NO number rather than an invented one.

cases.name: part with neither a sheet nor model codes
cases.why: The tenon-adapter pseudo-arm has no ordering data at all — the resolver must return nothing.

cases.name: pole accessories append after the ordering columns
cases.why: Options/accessories codes are appended in column order after every ordering segment — this is what Z2 makes the cache aware of.

cases.name: pole length and design come from the part, not a dropdown
cases.why: Which pole you picked already answers both; the parsed `design` column is polluted, so designCode/heightFt are read off the part (docs/part-numbers.md).

cases.name: multi-select code order is significant
cases.why: The same accessory codes in the opposite order print a different number — which is why config_hash must not sort them.

cases.name: DRX post top is held from the cut — no part number, in both languages
cases.why: Phase 0.12: this case used to pin the 'design resolves from part.family' rule on DRX. Tyler's 8/11 cut is GVX + TEX, so DRX now carries an editorial hold and resolves to NO number at all — a held product must never emit a spec-able SKU. That suppression is itself worth pinning cross-language: if the Python mirror forgot it, the generated PDF would print a number the browser refuses to show. The family-fallback rule it used to cover is still exercised by the TEX cases below, whose Design segment resolves the same way.

cases.name: TEX reproduces the spec sheet's own ordering example
cases.why: The 0.12 anchor case, hand-taken from the TEX sheet (Rev V01072026) rather than from our own output: WD-TEX-80-30-MV-5W-3T-NA-BK. Pins the Design/Lumen split AND the two finish segments at once — before 0.12 the merged columns could emit only one of Design/Lumen, and one finish code for both segments.

cases.name: TEX accent finish defaults to the housing finish
cases.why: An untouched accent must resolve to a real colour the customer picked, not '_': the sheet says the accent designation is always required. Mirrors how a slot finish falls back to the base config finish.

cases.name: TEX side mount still carries both finish segments
cases.why: 'For side mount fixtures, the mounting arm will match the housing color. Accent line finish designation is still required.' SMS must not drop the accent segment.

cases.name: TEX accent finish outside the sheet's colour column
cases.why: The TEX sheet prints 10 colours; the palette carries 13. A finish the column omits must fall back to the palette code (SA), never to '_' — and that fallback must behave identically in both languages.

cases.name: Banner arm kit resolves BA24 from the default panel (CR-OPT-15)
cases.why: Tyler 8/14 (Puddy check A): the BAX placeholder is retired from the printed number — the arm code is BA18/BA24/BA30, following each instance's banner panel width. A checked kit whose placement box was never touched uses the catalog's default panel (24x48 -> BA24). Both languages must resolve per instance identically.

cases.name: Two banners of different sizes print two different arm codes (CR-OPT-15)
cases.why: Size resolution is PER INSTANCE, not per config: a 30x60 banner and an 18x36 banner on one pole print BA30 and BA18 — the one shape CR-OPT-07/10 (single-resolution) cannot express, which is why resolvesBySize exists.

cases.name: wall-mounted build — GVX on the WM1 wall bracket (Phase 0.21)
cases.why: The first pole-less assembly to resolve numbers. Two things are pinned: the FIXTURE picks up WHP3NP from the bracket's cordCode (CR-OPT-06: 'PM1 and future WM1/WM2/PC1 -> WHP3NP'), and the BRACKET resolves to null because WM1 is still Coming Soon pending Cole's CAD-mapping confirm. When that confirm lands and WM1 leaves Coming Soon, this case must be REGENERATED and the arm becomes WP-WM1-WM-BK (the fit segment is the arms sheet's fixed wall-plate code, not the '_' every pole bracket prints) - see the un-hold procedure in docs/part-numbers.md.

cases.name: MVX — the sheet's own published ordering example (Rev. V08182026 p8)
cases.why: The MVX sheet prints Ex: WD-MVX-80-30-MV-5W-3T-BK-SRG27710. Reproducing a sheet's own example byte-exact in BOTH languages is the ingest rule for a newly-corrected matrix — it is the one string the manufacturer has already published.

cases.name: MVX with the FT Decorative Finial Top (Phase 0.21)
cases.why: Cole's 9/3 re-export REMOVED the finial from the MVX body, and the sheet says why: it is the accessory code FT (Available With 3T Mount Only). This pins that a finialled MVX orders as ...-3T-BK-FT, so the geometry split and the part number tell the same story.

cases.name: MVX pendant mount with the FB Decorative Finial Bottom (Phase 0.21)
cases.why: The mirror case: on a PM mount the finial hangs BELOW (FB, 'Available On PM Mount Only'). Pinned so the two mount-exclusive finial codes cannot be swapped without a failing test.
